messages.content: 你能計算從地球到一個新發現的距離為4.22光年的外行星，再到另一個距離第一顆外行星6.1光年的外行星，最後再回到距離第二顆外行星5.88光年的地球所需的時間嗎？假設真空中光的速度為299792458公尺/秒。

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years. This is a float type value.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

message.reasoning:
We need to calculate total travel time: Earth -> first exoplanet (distance 4.22 ly), then first exoplanet -> second exoplanet (distance 6.1 ly), then second exoplanet -> Earth (distance 5.88 ly). Sum distances: 4.22 + 6.1 + 5.88 = 16.2 ly. Then convert light-years to meters? Light-year is distance light travels in one year. So 1 ly = c * seconds per year. Seconds per year ~ 31557600 (Julian year). Use speed of light 299792458 m/s. So 1 ly = 299792458 * 31557600 ≈ 9.4607304725808e15 m. Multiply by 16.2 gives total meters. Then divide by speed of light to get seconds. But we can just compute time = sum distances * 1 year because light travels 1 ly in 1 year. So total time = 16.2 years. But maybe they want more precise: 16.2 years. If want days: 16.2*365.25=5920.05 days. Or hours etc.

But the tool expects distance_in_light_years and returns something. We can call the function with distance 16.2. It will return time? Let's see function signature: light_travel_time(distance_in_light_years: number, speed_of_light?: number) => any. Likely returns time in seconds or maybe in some format. We'll call it.
